patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Closely and Gong share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Comparison thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose Closely only if your buying job matches “LinkedIn + email outbound automation platform with enrichment, AI agents, and white-label ” rather than Gong's shape. Choose Gong only if your buying job matches “Conversation intelligence / revenue AI — per-user licenses + platform fee; custom proposal” rather than Closely's shape. Workflow advantage: Closely leans prospecting; Gong leans lead-management. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Closely and Gong share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Closely is LinkedIn + email outbound automation platform with enrichment, AI agents, and white-label options for agencies.; Gong is Conversation intelligence / revenue AI — per-user licenses + platform fee; custom proposal only (no public dollar list)..
- Workflow coverage skew: Closely-leaning prospecting vs Gong-leaning lead-management.
- Researched limits: Closely — Not a CRM deal-pipeline system of record.; Gong — Separate job from sales intelligence contact databases.

Limitations — Closely: Not a CRM deal-pipeline system of record.; Plans are gated by LinkedIn sender seats and enrichment/AI credit bundles.; Gong: Separate job from sales intelligence contact databases; Not a prospecting/enrichment data core.

Poor-fit cases: Closely is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Not a CRM deal-pipeline system of record. · Gong is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Separate job from sales intelligence contact databases · Avoid Closely if you actually need Gong's motion (Conversation intelligence / revenue AI — per-user licenses + platform fee; custo)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
